items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: one night at the old economy hall Chris was playing there and I just they made me sitting behind the drums

ctx.x: Faso I never knew Faso's right name I don't believe everybody knows his name Everybody knows him about Faso This year was two drums the only had was an old bass drum a snare drum and a crash cymbal no sax stands but in four cowbells and the very seldom he had a little tum-tum with it and he he was one of I think my idea was one of the best jazz drummers we had in all of us good timekeeper well that's the one I used to follow when like the first band when I used to before I even started with the Young Tuxedo band…
and how was that how was that band to play with how did you enjoy it

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: He used to play a lot with Chris Kelly and them different bands.

ctx.x: What kind of stuff did he play?
He was a pretty fair drummer. He used to play a lot with Chris Kelly and them different bands. Then we had another one with my favorite in them days was Faso.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: And the best group for me could play that number was Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: You mean, like that bar we went in, you know, to get drinks the other day, was that there then?

No, I can't remember, Jane, of that same place. No, I don't believe that section was there, no, because sometimes they may put, like, little private tables on our side, you know, put like tablecloths or something on it, or a piece of white cloth in front of it. But the place would be so jam-packed during them nights, you see, on both yards would be crowded. And I would say like the other night, the fifth day when we was making a recording, the voices say you could hear when you're playing like Kelly's Love, that…
And where did he play? Inside the hall or in the yard? In the yard.
